descripcion: At B1 you fix the simplest and most common verb-noun collocations: make a decision, have breakfast, take a shower. These verbs aren't freely interchangeable, and each noun in English has its own fixed verb partner to learn alongside it.

ejemplos.texto: I usually have breakfast at eight.
I need to make a decision soon.

notas: Have is the default verb for meals: have breakfast, have lunch, have dinner.
Make a decision and make a mistake use make, not do.
Take a shower and have a shower are both correct; take is more common in American English.

contraste.es: El español usa tomar para varias de estas colocaciones (tomar una decisión, tomar una ducha), lo que en inglés se reparte entre make, have y take según la palabra específica.

errores: Using do instead of have for meals.
Saying do a decision instead of make a decision.
Using make where have or take would be correct.
autochequeo: Is have used for meals, not do?
Is make used for decisions and mistakes, not do?
Have I used at least four different collocations?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on verb-noun collocations. Check the choice between have, make and take for each fixed expression, especially meals, decisions and mistakes. Do not rewrite the text.
